attributes.name: alert_group_type
attributes.markdownDescription:
Category of alert type based on the application or network layer and source of the test.

<!-- probed:static -->
The SDK's encoding drops this type's zero value (omitempty), so configuring false, 0 or "" silently becomes an omission.
<!-- /probed -->

<!-- probed:7.0.98-t1785764456095 -->
Values accepted here: `bgp`, `browser-session`, `cloud-enterprise`, `endpoint`.
Observed: the API assigns "cloud-enterprise" when this is omitted.
<!-- /probed -->

The applied group follows the alert type -- an http-server rule stores cloud-enterprise whatever is sent -- so the fixtures leave it to the server.

attributes.name: alert_type
attributes.markdownDescription:
Type of alert being triggered. In multi-layered tests, this value represents the layer the alert relates to. See [Alert Details](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/thousandeyes/retrieve-alert-details/) documentation for a list of possible values

<!-- probed:7.0.98-t1785764456095 -->
The API enforces this field's presence, which the specification does not declare.
<!-- /probed -->

attributes.name: description
attributes.markdownDescription: A description of the alert rule.

attributes.name: direction
attributes.markdownDescription:
Direction for applicable alert types (eg. path trace, End-to-End (Agent) etc.)

<!-- probed:static -->
The SDK's encoding drops this type's zero value (omitempty), so configuring false, 0 or "" silently becomes an omission.
<!-- /probed -->

Only valid for directional alert types (end-to-end agent/server); refused for http-server rules (live acceptance, 2026-08-03).

attributes.name: endpoint_agent_ids
attributes.markdownDescription:
An array of endpoint agent IDs associated with the rule (get `id` from `/endpoint/agents` API). This is applicable when `alertGroupType` is `browser-session`.

<!-- probed:7.0.98-t1785764967601 -->
Neither the update response nor a read returns this field: it is write-only in practice, and state carries the configured value.
<!-- /probed -->

attributes.name: endpoint_label_ids
attributes.markdownDescription:
An array of label IDs used to assign specific Endpoint Agents to the test (get `id` from `/endpoint/labels`). This is applicable when `alertGroupType` is `browser-session`.

<!-- probed:7.0.98-t1785764967601 -->
Neither the update response nor a read returns this field: it is write-only in practice, and state carries the configured value.
<!-- /probed -->

attributes.name: expression
attributes.markdownDescription:
The expression of the alert rule.

<!-- probed:7.0.98-t1785764456095 -->
The API enforces this field's presence, which the specification does not declare.
<!-- /probed -->

attributes.name: include_covered_prefixes
attributes.markdownDescription: Set true to include covered prefixes in the BGP alert rule. Only applicable to BGP alert rules.

attributes.name: is_default
attributes.markdownDescription:
If set to `true`, this alert rule becomes the default for its test type and is automatically applied to newly created tests with relevant metrics. Only one default alert rule is allowed per test type.

<!-- probed:7.0.98-t1785764967601 -->
Observed: the API assigns false when this is omitted from an update.
Omitting this field from an update resets it rather than preserving the stored value.
<!-- /probed -->

attributes.name: minimum_sources
attributes.markdownDescription:
The minimum number of agents or monitors that must meet the specified criteria to trigger the alert.

Exactly one of minimum_sources and minimum_sources_pct must be set (live probe, 2026-08-03).

<!-- probed:7.0.98-t1785764456095 -->
The API enforces this field's presence, which the specification does not declare.
<!-- /probed -->

attributes.name: minimum_sources_pct
attributes.markdownDescription:
The minimum percentage of all assigned agents or monitors that must meet the specified criteria to trigger the alert.

Exactly one of minimum_sources and minimum_sources_pct may be set; the generated fixtures carry minimum_sources.

attributes.name: id
attributes.markdownDescription:

attributes.name: sensitivity_level
attributes.markdownDescription: Used when `roundsViolatingMode` is set to `auto`. The default is `medium`. Higher sensitivity increases the likelihood of triggering alerts.
